newsitem.title: CHINA: China A share indices end up, B indices mixed.
newsitem.headline: China A share indices end up, B indices mixed.

text.p: China's A share indices continued their inexorable rise on Wednesday with the Shenzhen A index closing at a new high.
B indices, however, were mixed on profit-taking.
The Shenzhen A index rose 8.57 points or 1.63 percent to end at 533.78 on turnover of 21.3 billion yuan. But it failed to lift the B index which eased on profit-taking, analysts said.
After recording sharp gains over the last two days, the Shenzhen B share index fell 1.46 points or 0.79 percent to end at 182.74 on turnover of HK$233.63 million.
"The B index is still on its way up although it sagged today on profit-taking," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
New listings in Shenzhen scheduled for later this month are now limiting buying of existing listed stocks, brokers said.
"Some investors are holding back and waiting for the new shares," the Guotai analyst said.

Pesticide maker Hubei Sanonda Co Ltd, Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd and Nanjing Posts & Telecommunications Equipment Co Ltd have all announced they will each offer 100 million B shares for listing later this month.
The new counters are expected to perform well and analysts said they will help boost market sentiment.
"The new listings indicate that the government really is trying to expand the size of the market," the analyst said.
Shenzhen Nanshan Power Station Co Ltd was the sharpest loser in the B share market, down HK$0.23 or 4.22 percent to HK$5.22.

Shanghai B shares edged up on Wednesday on institutional buying of blue chips, but follow-up buying was limited with investors concerned that Beijing may move to control the irrepressible A share markets, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.236 points or 0.24 percent to 98.206 on volume of 43.563 million shares worth $29.583 million.

"If the government takes measures to cool down the over-speculative A share market, it will have a negative impact on the B share market since domestic investors have become a major force in the B shares," said one broker.
Eastern Communications was the star, surging $0.136 or 9.71 percent to $1.536 on volume of 1.9 million shares.
Shanghai Chlor Alkali Chemical was the most actively traded on institutional cross-trading, rising 0.002 or 0.53 percent to $0.388 on volume of 3.5 million shares.

Shanghai's A share market extended its bull run thanks to further inflows of hot money, but some institutions were seen liquidating their positions due to concerns over Beijing's attitude toward the market's upward momentum, brokers said.
The index rose 13.278 points or 0.86 percent to 1,562.650 points on volume of 1.1 billion worth 15.4 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index moved up 49.930 points or 1.14 percent to 4,413.047 points.
